Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

also adverb

also too, as well, me too

classical

Plin. Ep. 8.8.6: īnfrā etiam natāre concessum
Cic. Tusc. 5.100: nōn sōlum in praesentiā, sed etiam posterō diē

etiam

adverb

also, too; even

Adds a further fact or person, before or after the word: nōn sōlum (modo) … sed etiam, not only … but also. In a question, Etiamne …?: etiamne hoc negābis? (Plaut. Am. 2.2.128, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • quoque — also, too

    adverb · also used · classical · Ov. Rem. 104: crās quoque fīet idem; Liv. 1.9.3: urbēs quoque, ut cētera, ex īnfimō nāscī

    Always straight after the word it marks: mē quoque, me too (Hor. C. 1.16.22, Lewis & Short).

  • et — too, also (before the word)

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Stich. 2.1.44: Salvus sīs. — Et tū salvē. (Lewis & Short); Ter. Eun. 191: Et tū

    In greetings and answers: et tū, you too; et ego, so did I (Cic. Sen. 26). In narrative, Lewis & Short: frequent in Livy, rare in Cicero.

  • item — likewise, in the same way

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.52 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Div. 2.107 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Valē. — Et tū; numquid vīs aliud?

    Goodbye. — You too. Is there anything else you want?Ter. Eun. 190–191

  • dīcimus adsiduē 'crās quoque fīet idem'

    we keep saying, ‘it will be the same tomorrow too’Ov. Rem. 104

  • et ego fēcī quī litterās Graecās senex didicī

    so did I, who learned Greek as an old manCic. Sen. 26

See also too, same, only.
